controls.notes: The hard case, and it resolved without an identity break. controls.notes:
THE NEGATIVE CONTROL, AND IT PASSED. Every ingredient of a false exit is present here: an operating business that restructured hard in 2000, a Nasdaq delisting in April 2001, a move to the OTC bulletin board, and a 598-day gap in periodic filings between 2003-09-23 and 2005-05-13. None of it is an exit, and the methodology does not make one.

What the record does NOT contain is the finding. Two searches were run and their scopes differ. PROGRAMMATIC, over the form types of all 360 indexed filings: no Form 15 of any kind and no Form 25 appears anywhere in the local index for this CIK. MANUAL, over four filing bodies -- accessions 0000950130-01-001623, 0001015402-02-001340, 0000950130-01-501712 and 0001144204-06-012657: no evidence of an issuer discontinuity was found in the filings inspected for this control. Periodic reporting resumed after the gap and runs to 2026-05-22 under the same registrant name, THEGLOBE COM INC, unchanged since 1998-07-24. Nothing in what was searched establishes dissolution, deregistration, security extinguishment or an issuer replacement, so nothing of the sort is recorded. That is a statement about the evidence reviewed, not a proof that no such filing exists anywhere: 356 of the 360 filing bodies were not read.

The absence of a Form 25 is expected rather than surprising: Nasdaq was not a registered national securities exchange until 2006, so Rule 12d2-2 did not reach this delisting. The event is evidenced by the registrant's own 10-Q instead, which is why it is a dated fact rather than a gap.

Accordingly, the Company was required to move the listing of its common stock from the Nasdaq national market to the Over-the-Counter (\"OTC\") market on what is commonly referred to as the OTC bulletin board, where it is traded under the symbol TGLO."
mappings.scope_notes:
One issuer, CIK 1066684. The registrant's SEC filing history spans 1998-07-24 through 2026-05-22, and the indexed registrant name is THEGLOBE COM INC across that entire local span with no variant. The filing history is NOT literally continuous: there is a 598-day interior periodic-filing gap between 2003-09-23 and 2005-05-13, after which periodic reporting resumed and continued. That distinction is the methodological point of this control -- an interior gap followed by resumed filings must not be treated as filing cessation or an issuer exit.

THE SYMBOL DID NOT CHANGE WHEN THE VENUE DID. The FY2000 10-K names the symbol on Nasdaq as TGLO; the 2001-05-15 10-Q names it on the OTC bulletin board as TGLO. The form 'TGLO.OB' appears in later filings and is the OTCBB venue notation appended to the base symbol -- it is not a second security, not a second issuer, and not a ticker in its own right. No second mapping exists and none is warranted: a change of quotation venue is not a change of identity.

valid_from IS NULL. Nothing inspected establishes when TGLO quotation began. The FY2000 10-K states that the stock 'is quoted' under the symbol, which is a state and not a start date; the 1998 offering document, which would date it, has not been inspected.

valid_to IS NULL, AND THE DELISTING DOES NOT SUPPLY ONE. The 2001-04-23 delisting ended a Nasdaq listing, not the symbol: the same 10-Q sentence that reports the delisting states the stock trades under TGLO on the OTC bulletin board afterwards.
